questions.prompt: A wheel's angular velocity changes from \(3.0\) to \(15.0\,\mathrm{rad\,s^{-1}}\) in \(4.0\,\mathrm{s}\). Find average angular acceleration.
At one instant, \(\omega=-4.0\,\mathrm{rad\,s^{-1}}\) and \(\alpha=+1.0\,\mathrm{rad\,s^{-2}}\). Is the angular speed increasing or decreasing?
questions.answer:
The signs are opposite:
\[
\omega\alpha=(-4.0)(+1.0)<0
\]
so the angular speed is decreasing.

questions.prompt: A point is \(0.50\,\mathrm{m}\) from an axis. If \(\alpha=6.0\,\mathrm{rad\,s^{-2}}\), find its tangential acceleration.
A wheel changes from \(+10\,\mathrm{rad\,s^{-1}}\) to \(-5.0\,\mathrm{rad\,s^{-1}}\) in \(3.0\,\mathrm{s}\). Find average angular acceleration.
questions.answer:
\[
\alpha_{\mathrm{av}}=\frac{-5.0-10}{3.0}=-5.0\,\mathrm{rad\,s^{-2}}
\]
The negative sign means the angular velocity changes in the negative direction.

questions.prompt: For \(\theta(t)=t^3-6t^2\), find when \(\alpha=0\), then state whether the wheel is instantaneously at rest then.
questions.answer:
\[
\omega(t)=3t^2-12t
\]
\[
\alpha(t)=6t-12
\]
\[
\alpha=0\Rightarrow t=2.0\,\mathrm{s}
\]
At that time,
\[
\omega(2.0)=3(2.0)^2-12(2.0)=-12\,\mathrm{rad\,s^{-1}}
\]
so the wheel is not instantaneously at rest.

questions.prompt: For \(\omega(t)=8-4t+t^2\), determine whether the rotation ever stops for \(t\ge0\). Use the result to interpret the angular speed.
questions.answer:
Check whether \(\omega=0\):
\[
t^2-4t+8=0
\]
The discriminant is
\[
(-4)^2-4(1)(8)=-16<0
\]
so there is no real stopping time. Since the parabola opens upward and has minimum \(\omega(2)=4\,\mathrm{rad\,s^{-1}}\), the angular speed remains positive.

questions.prompt: A wheel starts from rest with angular acceleration \(\alpha(t)=6.0-2.0t\) in \(\mathrm{rad\,s^{-2}}\). Find when angular speed is maximum, the maximum angular speed, and the angular displacement up to that instant. State the assumption behind the maximum condition.
questions.answer:
Starting from rest,
\[
\omega(t)=\int_0^t(6.0-2.0t')\,dt'=6.0t-t^2
\]
The angular speed is maximum when acceleration changes from positive to negative:
\[
\alpha(t)=0\Rightarrow 6.0-2.0t=0
\]
\[
t=3.0\,\mathrm{s}
\]
\[
\omega_{\max}=6.0(3.0)-3.0^2=9.0\,\mathrm{rad\,s^{-1}}
\]
The angular displacement is
\[
\Delta\theta=\int_0^3(6.0t-t^2)\,dt=18\,\mathrm{rad}
\]
Assumption: \(\omega\) stays positive up to this instant, so maximizing \(\omega\) also maximizes angular speed.

questions.prompt: For \(\omega(t)=\omega_0+\alpha_0t-\frac{1}{2}\beta t^2\) with \(\beta>0\), derive the condition for real stopping times and give the first positive stopping time when it exists.
questions.answer:
Stopping requires
\[
\omega_0+\alpha_0t-\frac{1}{2}\beta t^2=0
\]
or
\[
\beta t^2-2\alpha_0t-2\omega_0=0
\]
The discriminant condition is
\[
D=(-2\alpha_0)^2+8\beta\omega_0=4(\alpha_0^2+2\beta\omega_0)\ge0
\]
so
\[
\alpha_0^2+2\beta\omega_0\ge0
\]
The two candidate times are
\[
t=\frac{\alpha_0\pm\sqrt{\alpha_0^2+2\beta\omega_0}}{\beta}
\]
The first stopping time is the smallest positive candidate. If \(\omega_0>0\), this is
\[
t_{\mathrm{stop}}=\frac{\alpha_0+\sqrt{\alpha_0^2+2\beta\omega_0}}{\beta}
\]
The sign and positivity checks matter because real roots can still lie outside the physical time interval.
